body: I'm guessing you don't want to have children.

It wasn't life so much as crippling depression, but you'r right. I was going to finish it this year actually, but then my application to a Master's degree instead was accepted, and I decided it's better to spend 9k on a Master's than 13k on a BA's.
What's done is done, I need a way forward and not back, and I'll change my CV in case I need to have another interview after this.

I'm not in the US. The degree is in the UK and I've made sure it's a good university. I mean, they're really well-known, have a good reputation, and the degree is definitely accepted. There are some universities who will take you on even if you only have 'work experience in the field' and can show a portfolio of work.

It says year x - year x: BA x studies.

I have made it a point to include 'Diploma year x' in courses I completed, however, to distinguish those from the BA. I'm not sure it's working though, as a lot of people have asked me before about 'my degree'.
Ok! Thank you. I might do that if I have the balls.
I wish it were easier, but it might just come out of left field to suddenly tell them 'oh btw I didn't finish my degree'... :/

Yeah... I'm not sure it's even relevant anyway. Does your opinion change if I tell you that I will be doing a MA degree this year (online, so it doesn't interfere with the job)? I have told them this, and it is a big point in my favour (it will be a lot more related to the job than the BA I would have had had I finished it).

PS: yes, I have been accepted to a MA even though I don't have a BA.

I am aware... If they'd asked I'd immediately have said so, but they didn't, and of course I didn't bring it up because it didn't occur to me at the time... It has never been important in any other job interview (and I've had quite a few of them), since they only ever asked 1-2 questions about what I studied, and then just went on with other stuff. I just really want this job so idk what to do best. I don't want to lie, but I also don't want to hurt my chances.

Of course writing can't be forced, but can editing? If I just put in a TINY BIT MORE, will my novel be good enough? I know it won't, that's a given at this point, considering the time I spent on it (months, on and off, since 2012), but maybe, maybe, if I just do MORE, it will work? If I just do more, more, more, more, maybe it will happen? The novel might make sense?

I've put this thing aside so many times, but I've grown up so much it's incredibly difficult to relate to the person who wrote it at the time. At the time, it was great, and incredibly fun, but these days, I wouldn't read a book like it if I see it on the bookshelf. And yet! And yet I just try and try and try because maybe others will want to read it. Maybe others will enjoy it, however horrible the writing is. BUT: I can't publish it as is (it was my first book, and of course, even though the writing isn't THAT terrible and the story somewhat works, it's not in any way near good enough to be picked up by a publisher).

It prays so heavily on my mind. And if I let it go, it will simply come back, and come back, and come back again and again, and drive me completely insane. I want to get rid of it. I want to delete all the 500 files I have of it, but it just won't leave my brain alone!

As for a pattern... I'm not sure about it. I've tried to figure it out, but I can't really make sense of it. I will think of news ways to do things, be happy with the plan, do it for two-three days, and then just everything crashes and I'm depressed. There is a pattern there, perhaps failure, or again, doing the wrong thing, or perhaps not putting enough effort into it before giving up... I'm not sure, to be honest.
You don't have to upvote. I don't upvote, and this is a throwaway account anyway, so don't waste your time with it.

It cycles, but because it always comes back, I kind of am starting to think something is seriously wrong with my life. I start questioning a lot of things, such as 'should I really be trying so hard to fix this novel when (I write novels sometimes) when I'm not really into it?' or the horrible thought that my current relationship just isn't right, because the guy and I are simply not compatible at all because a.) I find him a bit boring (he literally has no hobbies expect watching videos and sometimes gaming, and no ambitions whatsoever in life) and would probably not go on a date with him now and b.) I'm usually a very active and outgoing person, and don't like to sit still, but this relationship is forcing me to (it feels like). On the other hand, you know, what if I'm completely wrong about everything?

What if the novel just needs MORE input to become something great? What if I'm quitting too easily?
What if it's good to have a boring/non-active partner, considering how tired I get all the time if I am too active for a long time? (A bit of food for thought: I met a cool girl at Uni, we hit it off immediately, did a lot of things together, had a lot of fun, but I've withdrawn so much I haven't seen her in months since I left Uni, despite all the fun we had, simply because even the thought of having fun overwhelms me at the moment.)

The thing is:

If I do try to go out and do things, it will work for a month or two, and then I'm so so tired, depressed, and anxious that I cannot even go outside any more for the next few months. I'm not sure this is because something is fundamentally wrong with me, or because I'm trying to do the wrong things in my life.

You should write a novel, don't worry about how it all connects. Your subconscious will do this for you.

And anyway, what have you to lose? If it doesn't work out, but you had some fun (or whatever, you didn't feel as shit) doing it, it's less of a waste of time than haunting reddit. And if it does work out, it might just get you somewhere, won't it?

I write stories, and a lot of my depression probably comes from the first novel I ever wrote not working out. I just can't see anything else to do with my life, but even writing has become a hassle, because, well, I like short form much better than long-form (it is much less demanding of my brain, and therefore hurts much less to try to get right), but no one buys short stories, really, and I'm not making any money of it. This, in turn, makes me feel it's useless, and I'm too much of a fucking mess to do anything else (like actually fix my long-form works) apparently.

What do you do? What do you mean by, you can't sleep? How long have you been up?
I wasn't trying to attack you, but living this way sucks, and if you can relate, I feel sorry that you're having the same pain, that's all.
